subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and must that cache live only inside one reviewer/run keyed by the full reviewed input?
rationale: The current bug is narrow and source-reproducible, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes when later requests bypass a fresh model review.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable approvals.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower behavior change with less cost reduction.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until maintainers have stronger security or live billing evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent GitHub commit metadata make this the strongest available route for the exec reviewer approval-boundary decision.
